title: Astronomy — The Heavens Declare God's Glory
description: Test your knowledge of God's amazing universe — the sun, moon, planets, stars, and galaxies!

questions.question: On which day of creation did God make the sun, moon, and stars?
questions.explanation: God created the sun, moon, and stars on Day 4 of creation (Genesis 1:14-19).

questions.question: Why is the sun's distance from Earth so important?
options: It is at just the right distance to support life
questions.explanation: God placed the sun at exactly the right distance — about 93 million miles — so Earth would have the right temperature to support life.

questions.question: How does the moon produce its light?
options: It has its own light source
It reflects the light of the sun
questions.explanation: The moon does not make its own light — it reflects the light of the sun, just as Christians are called to reflect Christ's light.

questions.question: Which planet is the largest in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.

questions.question: What makes Earth unique among all the planets?
options: It is the only planet designed to support life
It is closest to the sun
questions.explanation: God specifically designed Earth with the right temperature, atmosphere, and water to support life.

questions.question: According to Psalm 147:4, what does God do with every star?
options: He counts them and calls them each by name
questions.explanation: Psalm 147:4 says God 'determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name.'

questions.question: What is a galaxy?
options: A huge collection of stars, gas, dust, and planets
questions.explanation: A galaxy is a huge collection of stars, gas, dust, and planets held together by gravity. Our Milky Way has between 100 and 400 billion stars.

questions.question: Which astronaut took communion on the moon to honor God?
questions.explanation: Buzz Aldrin, a Christian, took communion on the moon's surface during the Apollo 11 mission and read from John 15:5.
